0.title: Why mostly at high latitudes?
0.body: Start with quiet wind. Most solar wind is deflected around the magnetosphere. Charged particles within it are guided along field lines into the high-latitude atmosphere, where collisions with atoms and molecules produce light. Auroras commonly form ovals around both magnetic poles, rather than glowing only at the poles themselves.

1.title: Increase pressure; keep the field northward
1.body: Compare Quiet and Strong solar wind: the dayside is compressed and the nightside tail changes shape. With a northward field, typical low-latitude dayside reconnection is less favorable, so auroras need not strengthen equally. Northward does not mean no reconnection or no auroras.

2.title: Keep the strength; turn the field southward
2.body: Choose Favorable for reconnection: strength stays at 85. A southward interplanetary field opposes the dayside geomagnetic field, favoring reconnection and energy input. The tail stores and releases energy, precipitation increases, and auroral ovals may expand. Real responses also depend on field magnitude, duration and the magnetosphere’s prior state.

guideHelp: Selecting a step loads its preset. After experimenting, select the step again to repeat the comparison.

legend.reconnection: Amber ring: schematic dayside reconnection; brighter means more favorable

colors: Auroral color depends on atmospheric composition, emission altitude and particle energy. Oxygen often emits green light around 100–200 km and red light higher up; nitrogen can produce blue, pink or purple. Green and pink in this diagram distinguish emission layers, not a rule that stronger wind makes redder auroras. Altitude ranges are approximate.
limits: The Sun, Earth, distances and emission heights are not to scale. The poles are symmetric magnetic poles; tilt, day–night differences and hemispheric asymmetry are omitted. Field lines, particle paths, reconnection markers and auroral extent are teaching illustrations, not solutions of plasma motion or magnetohydrodynamic equations. Reconnection changes magnetic connectivity and converts energy; field lines are not physical strings that break.
timeLimits: Controls update the illustration instantly, omitting travel time and delays in tail energy storage and release. Tail stretching is a visual cue for deformation and stored energy, not a tail-length law. This model cannot predict aurora visibility at a place or time.
